To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) shoot growth was enhanced in presence of S. gramulatus, (ii) the effect of S. gramunatus on shoot growth under dry conditions was more pronounced than under moist conditions, (iii) the activity of secreted enzymes was higher in presence of S.granulatus than in presence of any other ECM species, and (iv) the effect of species richness on seedling growth was not significant.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of ECM fungi on the performance of P. sylvesteris under two different watering regimes.
the role of species composition of ectomycorrhiza fungi in the growth response of Pinus sylvetris to drought.
the question whether the species richness or species identity of ectomycorrhiza-forming fungi has a positive effect on growth of Pinus sylves-tris seedlings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the species richness of the ECM fungal community does not affect the growth of P. syvestris seedlings under drought stress conditions.
S. granulus may be a good candidate to inoculate P. sylvestris seedlings under moist conditions.

ECM fungal communities may affect tree seedling performance in different ways, depending on the tree species, ECM fungal species and environmental conditions, and that the species richness of ectomycorrhiza per se may not be the only factor to explain the effect of ECM fungi on tree performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the positive effects of ECM fungi on tree seedling growth are species-specific and context-dependent.

the ECM fungus S. granulus is the most effective species in enhancing P. sylvesrtis seedling growth under moist conditions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of ECM fungi on seedling performance depends on species identity and environmental conditions.
ECM species richness does not seem to be beneficial for seedling performance.
the positive effect of S.granulatus on shoot biomass is context-dependent, and that this species is more likely to enhance shoot growth in moist rather than dry conditions.
